readout_other: 3D MR-compatible hand accelerometry (tremor power in 2-20 Hz band); Clinical Rating Scale for Tremor (CRST A-B); MR thermometry
direction_notes: 5 of 9 patients (55%) were responders with a substantial and sustained decrease in tremor power (up to ~98% reduction) after VIM and/or DRT stimulation; 4 of 9 (45%) were non-responders who typically showed an increase in tremor power immediately after sonication.
safety_notes: No significant thermal rise was observed on MR thermometry during neurostimulation sonications; temperature at target was 37.2 +/- 1.4 degC vs 36.8 +/- 1.4 degC at a control voxel 3 cm away.

target.label: ventral intermediate nucleus of the thalamus (VIM)

timing.protocol_description: Four sonication patterns (modes 1-4) were tested; all lasted 35 s (three 5 s bursts followed by a 10 s off period), except Mode 4 (9-point 1.5x1.5 mm grid, total 54 s, 1 s pulse trains repeated every 9 s). Modes 1 and 2 achieved a high duty cycle (one-third) via a long-duration/low-PRF or short-duration/high-PRF burst respectively; Modes 3 and 4 used a low duty cycle (5%). For VIM, patients typically received modes 1, 2 and 3 in sequence; each pulse lasted less than 30 ms.

DRT was stimulated using the low duty cycle (5%) mode 3 (35 s total: three 5 s bursts + 10 s off) and, in some patients, mode 4 (a 9-point 1.5x1.5 mm grid around the target, 1 s pulse trains per point, total 54 s). Patients typically moved from VIM stimulation (modes 1-3) to DRT stimulation with mode 3, then mode 4 to cover a larger zone.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Nine patients with ET, refractory to medical treatments and eligible for TUS thalamotomy were included in this study and accepted for treatment with the Insightec’s Exablate Neuro Magnetic Resonanceguided Focused Ultrasound (MRgFUS) device [72,73] at the Paris Brain Institute (ICM, Paris, France).
source_quotes.blinding: The pulsing patterns were applied in a blind order for both the patient and the neurologist.
source_quotes.readout_other: Tremor severity was evaluated using 3D MR-compatible accelerometers taped on the back of both hands during a standard tremoric posture [66].
source_quotes.safety_notes: MR thermometry during neurostimulations showed no significant thermal rise, supporting a mechanical effect.

Table 3 reports per-sonication pressure (~0.79-0.99 MPa) and ISPTA (~0.1-0.7 W/cm2) values for DRT sonications that vary across patients; only the main-text representative value is captured here.

The paper states the pressure was 'adjusted to produce' a target value inside the brain via the Insightec system but does not explicitly state whether this in-situ value is from simulation, derating, or measurement in the main text.
